rv.q: This is British theatre operating at the very top of its game.
The wit and larky intellectualism on display in Tom Stoppard’s 1974 play will have you smirking with pleasure.
McDonald delivers a light-touch with Joyce, something that aids in the profundity of his this most excellent speech.

Sense it seems can be overrated, and those grappling too hard for a clear narrative or stable dramaturgy may be disappointed. Henry Carr is a British diplomat living in Zurich during the First World War, at a time when the city itself was a wash of intriguing creative personalities, many of which become muddled in his mind.

Tom Stoppard is one of those playwrights that make you feel clever just by buying a ticket. "Look" your ticket tells the world, "I'm a person who will appreciate a wordy play based on an intellectual conceit" Those tickets sell like hot cakes to London's intelligentsia.
